question.problem:
In a technical support call center, waiting times are normally distributed with a mean of $15$ minutes and a standard deviation of $3$ minutes. The conversation times are normally distributed with a mean of $10$ minutes and a standard deviation of $4$ minutes. The time to solve a problem is the sum of the waiting time and the conversation time. What is the probability that it took more than $30$ minutes to solve the problem of a randomly selected caller? You may assume that waiting and conversation times are independent.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.0\,$ | $\,0.8413\,$ | $\,0.8438\,$ | $\,0.8461\,$ | $\,0.8485\,$ | $\,0.8508\,$ |
| $\,1.1\,$ | $\,0.8643\,$ | $\,0.8665\,$ | $\,0.8686\,$ | $\,0.8708\,$ | $\,0.8729\,$ |
| $\,1.2\,$ | $\,0.8849\,$ | $\,0.8869\,$ | $\,0.8888\,$ | $\,0.8907\,$ | $\,0.8925\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ denote the waiting time, and let $Y$ denote the conversation time. We want to find 

$$
P(X+Y>30).
$$

Since $X$ and $Y$ are independent random variables such that $X∼N(15,{3}^{2})$ and $Y∼N(10,{4}^{2})$, then 

$$
\begin{aligned}X+Y & ∼N(15+10,{3}^{2}+{4}^{2}) \\  & ∼N(25,25).\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variable $X+Y$ is normally distributed with mean $\mu =25$ and standard deviation $\sigma =\sqrt{25}=5.$

In order to find $P(X+Y>30),$ we convert $X+Y$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X+Y>30) & =P(Z>\frac{30-25}{5}) \\  & ≈P(Z>1) \\  & =1-P(Z\le 1) \\  & =1-Φ(1)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(1)≈0.8413.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X+Y>30) & =1-Φ(1) \\  & ≈1-0.8413 \\  & ≈0.1587.\end{aligned}
$$
